items.title: Alan Broadbent interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 26, 2023
items.q: So they heard me and heard I was an arranger and I went out with Woody.

ctx.x: It’s fairly profound. Did you have a passion to play and tour with a big band? Or was that one of the things that came up and you said, and speaking of Woody Herman, “Well yeah, I’ll try that. I need a gig.”

Well how I joined Woody is that a great pianist/arranger Nat Pierce and the great drummer, they were both with Woody back in the heyday ‘60s I mean — Jake Hanna and Nat came down to hear me play at a club and it was the end of my last year and the semester and I needed a way to extend my visa and here was an opportunity. So they heard me and heard I was an arranger and I went out with Woody. So that was that.

Most of the guys, you could correct me if I’m wrong, but most of the band, as time went by, became quite a bit younger than Woody. And did he take — embrace the opportunity to be introduced to music that he might not have normally considered for his band?

items.title: 52220_Woody Herman oral history interview
items.q: And his writing had a great deal to do with where we started to move.

ctx.x: And his writing had a great deal to do with where we started to move. And what I would attempt and what we would all attempt. And --
I can't remember the -- how long did Bill Chase stay with you?
